text: 如何反驳支持劳务派遣合法化的人？
en: How do you rebut people who support the legalisation of labour dispatch?

text: 你会从事劳务派遣工作吗？
en: Would you take up labour dispatch work?

text: 如何反驳支持延迟退休的人？
en: How do you rebut people who support delayed retirement?

text: 你会让自己工作到65岁才领取退休金吗？
en: Would you let yourself work until the age of 65 before collecting your pension?

text: 如何反驳支持外卖网约车平台不与雇佣人员签署劳动合同的人？
en: How do you rebut those who support food-delivery and ride-hailing platforms not signing employment contracts with their workers?

text: 你送外卖会办理个体工商牌照吗？
en: Would you obtain an individual business licence to deliver food?

text: 额，好像，会的。
en: Er, probably, yes.

text: 其实这些人并不想要卖淫合法不合法，因为现在嫖娼并不难，没有哪个男人很难找到嫖娼资源。
en: Actually, these people don't really care whether prostitution is legal or not, because finding paid sex isn't difficult nowadays—no man has much trouble finding sources of paid sex.

text: 世界卫生组织早就统计到了国内有几百万性服务人员。
en: The World Health Organisation long ago counted several million sex workers within the country.

text: 这些人的本意是希望可以通过合法化把性服务的价格打下来，让性资源变得触手可得，自己就是皇帝，花不到四位数就能享受颜值八分的女生，是这个意思，自己就不用花钱追求女生了。
en: The real intention of these people is that they hope legalisation can drive down the price of sex services, make sexual resources readily available, make themselves emperors, and enjoy girls rated eight out of ten in looks for under four figures—that is the idea: they wouldn't have to spend money chasing girls.

text: 类似平均下来一天花不到一百块就能享受一个妙龄女子。
en: Similarly, on average one could enjoy a young woman for under a hundred yuan a day.

text: 并且还希望合法化能保证质量，这样的话，这些所谓的仙人跳局、敲诈和服务态度恶劣都会消失，这样就很好。
en: And they also hope legalisation can guarantee quality, so that these so-called honeytraps, extortion and poor service attitudes would disappear—that would be just fine.

text: 但是管理是需要成本和金钱维持的，并且嫖客自己都把性服务者看的很低贱，更不要提其他人如何看待性服务者了。
en: But management requires money and resources to sustain, and the clients themselves regard sex workers as very lowly—let alone how others view sex workers.

text: 合法化实话实说是吃力不讨好的事情，既要付出高昂的经济管理成本、对于管理者来说收益很有限，还增加了高昂的治安成本。
en: To be honest, legalisation is a thankless endeavour: it demands high economic and management costs, yields very limited returns for those managing it, and adds steep public-order costs.

text: 因为嫖娼的钱和成瘾性还是来的太慢了，嫖客还能理智的货比三家，挑选便宜的性工作者，这是资本不愿意看到的买方市场。
en: Because the money from paid sex and its addictive pull still arrive too slowly, clients can still rationally compare options and pick cheaper sexworkers—this is a buyer's market that capital has no interest in seeing.

text: 市场是不断逐利的，一旦合法化竞争激烈后，很多场所为了吸引更多的顾客，就会上赌博和毒品，黄赌毒不分家就是这个道理。
en: Markets are forever profit-driven; once legalisation intensifies competition, many venues, to draw in more customers, will introduce gambling and drugs. This is precisely why prostitution, gambling and drugs are inseparable.

text: 那么治安成本就会飞速上升。
en: Then public-order costs will rise rapidly.

text: 现在的不合法化，符合不嫖娼的人的利益，他们也不用承担额外的治安成本，也符合性工作者的利益，他们可以价格调高赚取更多的钱，甚至威胁嫖客拿到更多的额外报酬。
en: The current state of illegality serves the interests of those who don't buy sex—they needn't bear extra public-order costs—and it also serves the interests of sex workers, who can raise their prices to earn more, even threatening clients to extract extra payment.

text: 毕竟这玩意是吃青春饭的。
en: After all, this line of work trades on youth.

text: 唯一损害的就是瓢虫的利益了。
en: The only ones harmed are the interests of the ladybirds.

text: 但是部分标准低的瓢虫也无所谓，毕竟有钱就去嫖娼，没钱不去就是了，或者找便宜年纪大的性工作者。
en: But some ladybirds with low standards don't care either; after all, if they have money they go buy sex, and if not they simply don't, or they find cheaper, older sex workers.

text: 本来瓢虫这个群体就是分裂的，大多数人不过嘴上说说罢了。
en: As it is, the ladybird group is itself divided; most people just talk the talk.

text: 唯一最不满的瓢虫是那种有点小钱，有点优越感，有点小标准，很抠又很挑剔，想要廉价享受质量比较好的性服务者。
en: The only ladybirds who are most dissatisfied are those with a bit of money, a bit of a superiority complex, a few petty standards, who are stingy yet picky, and who want to enjoy relatively good-quality sex workers on the cheap.

text: 但是这个群体一方面也没有太多钱，也没啥油水可以压榨，另一方面为了少数群体得罪大多数群体，基本上没人会这么做，所以就直接忽略了。
en: But on the one hand this group doesn't have much money and there's no real profit to squeeze out of them; on the other hand, no one would offend the majority for the sake of a minority, so they are simply ignored.

text: PS:在日本嫖娼也并不合法，警察也抓过性服务者，所谓的性工作者只是睁一只眼闭一只眼。
en: PS: Buying sex is also not legal in Japan; the police have arrested sex workers, and the so-called sex workers are merely tolerated, with one eye shut.

text: 如果合法的话，会有无数山区的妇女或者重男轻女家庭中的女孩，被“自愿”出来从事。
en: If it were legal, countless women from mountainous areas or girls from families that favour boys over girls would be 'voluntarily' pushed into this line of work.

text: 冷知识，讨厌嫖虫和支持卖淫合法化是可以并存的。
en: Fun fact: disliking johns and supporting the legalisation of prostitution can coexist.

text: 就像我很讨厌你这样在和别人正常沟通的时候，会忽然开始蛮不讲理的人【不嫖娼会死吗请问？
en: Just like I really dislike people like you who, in the middle of a normal conversation with others, suddenly start acting unreasonably 【Does one die without buying sex, may I ask?

text: 】，但我也会支持每个人都有言论自由。
en: 】, but I would still support everyone having freedom of speech.

text: 你以为的强迫劳动：
en: What you imagine forced labour to be:

text: 需要一个手眼通天的地头蛇，打通公检法，手底下数十个打手青皮，人身控制 + 暴力胁迫。
en: It requires a powerful local boss with reach into every corner, who has the police, procuratorate and courts all in his pocket, with dozens of enforcers and thugs under his command, plus bodily confinement and violent coercion.

text: 实际的强迫劳动：
en: What forced labour actually is:

text: 一句 "不给你毕业证" 就够了。
en: A single line—'We won't give you your graduation certificate'—is enough.

text: 你猜如果合法化了，他们会强迫学生到哪实习？
en: Guess where they'd force students to do their internship if it were legalised?

text: 不用反驳，反正在中国大陆是不可能合法的，它们pc被抓就是犯法，你和潜在罪犯有什么好辩论的。
en: No need to rebut; in any case it can never be legalised on the Chinese mainland. When they get caught for patronising prostitutes, that's an offence—what's there to debate with a potential criminal?

text: 人无法在地上创立天国。
en: Man cannot build the Kingdom of Heaven upon the earth.

text: 用性服务合法化来确保性服务工作者都是自愿且受到法律保护这件事就是典型的“在地上创立天国”。
en: Using the legalisation of sex services to guarantee that all sex workers are there of their own free will and protected by law is a textbook example of 'building the Kingdom of Heaven upon the earth'.

text: 所有喜欢玩你法我笑梗的人，都没资格支持卖淫合法化。
en: Everyone who likes to trot out the 'your law, my laugh' meme has no right to support the legalisation of prostitution.

text: 有个疑问: 所谓【卖淫合法化】，重点是不是应该放在【合法化】上？
en: A question occurs to me: with the so-called 【legalisation of prostitution】, shouldn't the emphasis be placed on 【legalisation】?

text: 如果你做不到真正的【合法化】也就是【法律治理】，那你所谓的卖淫合法不合法还有啥区别？
en: If you can't achieve true 【legalisation】—that is, 【rule of law】—then what difference is there between your so-called legal or illegal prostitution?

text: 那样的话，跟我们目前处于灰色地带商K的区别是什么…
en: If so, what difference is there from the grey-area business KTVs we currently have…

text: 没区别啊。
en: No difference at all.

text: 那当然只会让社会变得更混乱咯。
en: Then of course it would only make society more chaotic.

text: 一个没有做到法治的地方，你跟我说合法化是不是有点脱了裤子放屁，多此一举？
en: In a place that hasn't achieved rule of law, isn't talking to me about legalisation a bit like dropping your trousers just to fart—utterly superfluous?

text: 就好比，本来贪污是“不合法”的，虽然也挡不住大家前腐后继，也挡不住普遍性贪污——但是终归有这么个形同虚设的标准。
en: It's like how corruption is 'illegal'—yet that can't stop people from tumbling into it one after another, nor stop it from being widespread—but in the end there is at least this nominal, toothless standard.

text: 现在有人提出“合法化”了，
en: Now someone proposes 'legalisation',

text: 可是这里的“合法化”，根本不是“法制”，
en: but this 'legalisation' is simply not 'rule of law',

text: 恰恰只是一个法律失效环境下的借口和说辞罢了，
en: but is merely an excuse and a pretext in an environment where the law has failed,

text: 【如果你做不到真正的法制，那你所谓的合法化就是纯扯淡，就是指鹿为马】
en: 【If you cannot achieve true rule of law, then your so-called legalisation is pure nonsense—it is calling a deer a horse】

text: 说白了就是“我管不了你们了，以后彻底摆烂不管了，你贪污是合法的了，放心贪吧”
en: Put plainly, it means 'I can't control you lot anymore; from now on I'm completely giving up and won't manage you, your corruption is now legal—go ahead and embezzle without worry'

text: 引发这个思考的，是我突然意识到我呆过5年的澳洲，其实是合法窑子的，也有合法赌场，甚至还有某些合法吸毒所（存疑）
en: What sparked this reflection was my sudden realisation that Australia, where I lived for five years, actually has legal brothels, legal casinos, and even some legal drug-consumption sites (doubtful).

text: 但是我似乎也没怎么见过听过这些，现实生活中并不会感到有什么区别。
en: But I seem to have rarely seen or heard of these things; in real life one doesn't feel any difference.

text: 这么多来澳洲留学的，很多人都不知道澳洲有合法窑子和赌场。
en: Of the many who come to study in Australia, a great many don't even know Australia has legal brothels and casinos.

text: 更没有什么比如澳洲人天天逛窑子或者赌博，男盗女娼遍地了，盗匪横行了，绑架妇女了，强迫卖淫了，
en: Let alone any notion that Australians visit brothels or gamble every day, that thieves and whores are everywhere, that bandits run rampant, that women are kidnapped, that prostitution is forced—

text: 澳洲男人都不好好上班，都去赌场碰运气，
en: Australian men don't properly hold down their jobs and all go to casinos to try their luck,

text: 澳洲女人都不好好上班，都被抓到窑子卖淫，
en: Australian women don't properly hold down their jobs and are all dragged to brothels to sell sex,

text: 照某些人的意思，那每年去澳洲留学的几十万留学生，
en: by some people's logic, then those hundreds of thousands of students who go to Australia to study each year,

text: 那不得男的都嫖娼赌博，女的都被抓到窑子卖淫兼职，
en: wouldn't the men all be patronising prostitutes and gambling, and the women all dragged to brothels to sell sex on the side,

text: 进一步的，去澳洲留学就等于要被噶腰子了…
en: and further still, going to study in Australia would mean having your kidneys harvested…

text: 所以我很好奇的是，大家的关注重点似乎错了？
en: So what I'm very curious about is this: has everyone's focus of attention seemingly been misplaced?

text: 我当然不希望我们社会变成泰国那样污水横流的窑子社会，
en: Of course I don't want our society to become a brothel-ridden society like Thailand, with filth flowing in its streets,

text: 但是…
en: But…

text: 既然你说的是【合法化】，那么你最起码得先存在【法制】吧？
en: Since what you're talking about is 【legalisation】, then at the very least you must first have 【rule of law】, right?

text: 如果你根本做不到【法制】，你所谓的卖淫合法化当然只能跟泰国一样呗？
en: If you fundamentally can't achieve 【rule of law】, then your so-called legalisation of prostitution can only end up like Thailand, can't it?

text: 所以泰国有【法制】吗？
en: So does Thailand have 【rule of law】?

text: 而且泰国法律可根本不承认卖淫合法化哦，不也一样窑子遍地吗。
en: Besides, Thai law doesn't recognise the legalisation of prostitution at all—yet brothels are still everywhere, aren't they?

text: 所以重点你们就搞错了，你们用一堆落后缺乏法制的国家，来论述如果“合法化”了会有多么糟糕，那你说的当然没错，那些地方即便不合法化也一样很糟糕，“合法化”了只会更糟糕
en: So your focus is wrong. You use a bunch of backward countries that lack rule of law to argue how awful things would be if 'legalised'. Well, you're not wrong—those places are just as awful even without legalisation, and 'legalisation' would only make them worse.

text: 这也是我为什么也不支持我们这里【合法化】，
en: This is also why I too do not support 【legalisation】 here,

text: 因为根本没意义，我们这里就根本没做到【法制】，也就无从谈起【合法化】。
en: because it's utterly meaningless—we simply haven't achieved 【rule of law】 here, so 【legalisation】 is out of the question.

text: 但是，如果一个国家有像样的【法制】，比如澳大利亚，加拿大，并不会因为所谓【卖淫合法化】就像某种道德挂帅的朋友以为的那样，变成泰国那种“男盗女娼”的危险毒窝。
en: But if a country has proper 【rule of law】—say Australia or Canada—it won't, because of so-called 【legalisation of prostitution】, turn into a dangerous den of vice like Thailand, with 'men as thieves and women as whores' everywhere, as some friends who are obsessed with morality imagine.

text: 毕竟，同属于祖国的香港，澳门，可都是有不同程度地黄赌毒合法化哦。
en: After all, Hong Kong and Macau, both part of the same motherland, each have prostitution, gambling and drugs legalised to varying degrees, you know.
